title: From Systems of Record to Systems of Context — Omri Bruchim & Tomer Ast, monday.com
talk_summary: monday.com describes building a 'world model' of each user by precomputing two layers offline: a slow engine that distills weeks of activity into a durable profile (persona, routines, collaborators, goals) and a fast engine that recomputes live signals over a short recent window, merged into a served context view. The core claim is that the bottleneck is not retrieval or context-window size but precomputed understanding of how entities relate, so it must be built ahead of time rather than at question time.

takeaways.technique: Precompute context offline instead of at request time
takeaways.what_they_do: Both engines precompute data structures, signals, and patterns ahead of time; at serve time only a thin slice of recent-activity logic is recomputed and the rest is served from the prebuilt model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Both engines premputee on top of that offline and ahead of time... a thin slice of logic is recomputed for recent activity

takeaways.what_they_do: A slow engine over weeks distills durable per-entity profiles (patterns, routines, collaborators, goals) that get reinforced over time; a fast engine over a short window recomputes live signals (what's urgent, what changed) and the two are merged into one served view.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A slow engine that runs on a long time window and learns the user and their work and a fast engine that reads what's happening right now

takeaways.technique: Durable distilled profile of recurring patterns
takeaways.what_they_do: Patterns mined from history are distilled into a durable profile that is reinforced each time it holds, rather than being re-derived per query.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Those patterns get distilled into a durable profile and every time a profile holds it's reinforced.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each data source is isolated so a bad feed can't break the rest; at serve time part of the context is verified against live data while the rest falls back to the last verified context, so it degrades rather than fails.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Sources are isolated so a bad feed can't break the rest... it degrades gracefully, but it doesn't fail.

takeaways.what_they_do: The fast engine computes live signals over current state — what's overdue, what's suddenly urgent, who's been pulled in — so the agent can decide when to be proactive and when to stay silent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's able to understand when and how it should be proactive and notify the user and when it should stay silent.

takeaways.technique: Treat the context model as testable architecture
takeaways.what_they_do: They frame the data model as an architecture that can be enriched, tested, and improved over time, and explicitly name its failure modes (trailing live world, cold start, built-in signal bias, noise vs. importance).
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is an architectural design that we can enrich and test and improve over time
